biomarkers.name: HPV / p16
biomarkers.type: HPV-specific testing, including ISH / p16 IHC
biomarkers.prevalence: HPV-negative by definition; usually p16-negative, although discordant HPV and p16 results occur
biomarkers.clinical_use: Distinguishes HPV-independent from HPV-associated disease. p16 IHC is the standard surrogate used for AJCC 8 oropharyngeal staging, with positivity defined by moderate-to-strong nuclear and cytoplasmic staining in at least 70% of tumor cells. p16 status is not perfectly equivalent to transcriptionally active HPV status; HPV-specific testing is appropriate in selected settings. HPV-negative disease generally has worse prognosis.

biomarkers.name: TP53
biomarkers.prevalence: Approximately 80–85% in HPV-negative HNSCC cohorts, including TCGA; this is not a separately established prevalence for HPV-negative oropharyngeal SCC
biomarkers.clinical_use: Major recurrent driver alteration. Some TP53 mutation classes are associated with adverse outcomes, but TP53 is not a routinely validated standalone prognostic or treatment-selection biomarker in this disease. No established TP53-directed standard therapy.

biomarkers.name: CDKN2A
biomarkers.type: inactivation through deletion, mutation, or promoter methylation
biomarkers.prevalence: Frequently inactivated in HPV-negative HNSCC; prevalence depends on the alteration types and assay included. A 50–70% estimate should not be presented as the prevalence of genomic loss alone or as a verified HPV-negative oropharyngeal SCC-specific figure.
biomarkers.clinical_use: Common tumor-suppressor alteration; may inform eligibility for CDK4/6 inhibitor trials. Not an established standalone prognostic biomarker or validated predictor of CDK4/6 inhibitor benefit in routine HNSCC care.

biomarkers.name: PD-L1 (CPS)
biomarkers.prevalence: Variable by cohort, assay, and CPS cutoff; no single established HPV-negative oropharyngeal SCC-specific prevalence
biomarkers.clinical_use: In the United States, CPS ≥1 supports first-line pembrolizumab monotherapy for metastatic or unresectable recurrent HNSCC. Pembrolizumab with platinum and fluorouracil is a first-line option regardless of PD-L1 CPS. PD-L1 is not a requirement for every checkpoint-inhibitor indication; requirements vary by regimen and jurisdiction.

biomarkers.name: EGFR
biomarkers.prevalence: EGFR expression is common in HNSCC. Frequently cited figures above 90% derive from broad HNSCC series and should not be treated as a verified overexpression prevalence for HPV-negative oropharyngeal SCC.
biomarkers.clinical_use: Target of cetuximab (anti-EGFR). EGFR IHC expression or overexpression is not a validated predictive biomarker for cetuximab benefit in HNSCC, and testing is not required for treatment selection.

histomorphological_subtype.primary_pattern: Usually conventional keratinizing SCC, resembling other HPV-independent UAT SCCs; nonkeratinizing or poorly differentiated morphology can also occur, so morphology alone does not establish HPV status
variants: moderately or poorly differentiated (histologic grades, not distinct morphologic variants)
histomorphological_subtype.grading: Traditional SCC differentiation grading may be reported, but its independent prognostic value is limited. HPV-negative disease generally has worse prognosis than HPV-associated disease; stage groups from their separate AJCC 8 staging systems are not directly interchangeable.

tumor_microenvironment.immune_context: Often less T-cell-inflamed than HPV-associated disease at the cohort level, but heterogeneous; immune-excluded and immune-desert phenotypes occur and are not universal
tumor_microenvironment.stromal_features: Desmoplastic stroma may be present, similar to other conventional head and neck SCCs, including oral cavity SCC

cellular_states_and_lineage.cell_of_origin: Presumed basal/progenitor squamous epithelial cells of the oropharyngeal mucosa; the precise initiating cell population is not definitively established
cellular_states_and_lineage.developmental_lineage: Squamous epithelial lineage; embryologic contribution varies by oropharyngeal subsite. A uniform assignment to 'endoderm — pharyngeal arch' is overly simplistic.
cellular_states_and_lineage.differentiation_state: Often keratinizing squamous with classical squamous maturation, but poorly differentiated and nonkeratinizing appearances also occur; this is not an absolute distinction from HPV-associated disease
cellular_states_and_lineage.lineage_plasticity: Field cancerization from tobacco/alcohol exposure is relevant but is not itself lineage plasticity. Epithelial–mesenchymal and other differentiation-state changes have been described in HNSCC, without defining a unique HPV-negative oropharyngeal SCC lineage-plasticity program.
